source_note: Doane, 'Comparing wins above replacement across baseball history', arXiv 2026 (Michael Doane, Independent Researcher, Cary NC; ORCID 0009-0003-0521-8981), 75 pages (33 text + supplement). Introduces iWAR (WAR from historical Retrosheet play-by-play; runs-allowed RA + fielding-independent FIP versions) and benchmarks against bWAR/fWAR/run-based on identical team-seasons (common 1,471 team-seasons/79 years/1,441 franchise pairs; secondary bWAR 2,554/118 years). iWAR RA reconstruction MAE 3.695 vs bWAR 4.724/fWAR 4.744 (~22% reduction), surviving scalar calibration; PythagenPat beats every WAR (3.263); next-season replay flips RA-fWAR sign after calibration on identical rows; advantage concentrated early history, shrinks with broader coverage; neural ensemble worse than ridge (10.163 vs 9.946). Key concepts: reconstruction-vs-replay (Shmueli description/prediction), run-expectancy batting weights, FIP 13/3/2 numerator, replacement conservation (sum WAR=0.206 sum G), fixed map y-hat=0.294+WAR/G, PythagenPat gamma=[(RS+RA)/G]^0.285, 5000-draw 5-year calendar-block bootstrap (Künsch), MSE accounting identity, conserving pitching-fielding transfer (team-total invariant -> individual credit not identifiable from team reconstruction). Data integrity: discrepancies retained without inferred repair, missing retained as missing, FanGraphs Statcast retroactive revisions; conditional intervals omit method-development/source-revision/coefficient-fitting uncertainty; learned study amended after constant-detector defect. Extracted faithfully (not a derivative summary). Equations (event run value, FIP, replacement conservation, credited fraction/fixed map, Pythagorean/PythagenPat, calibration regression, MSE identity) printed in math font that extracts garbled; reconstructed in labeled LaTeX and flagged here and in assumptions. Domain math matches catalog (baseball sabermetrics / valuation / prediction evaluation; not football). Directly isomorphic to GSE's EP kernel, description-vs-prediction evaluation, calibration-map fix, dependence-aware clustered inference, simple-baseline comparator, and attribution-identifiability limit. Code github MRDOANE/iwar-historical-benchmark, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23455100. No sportsbook lines/spreads/totals/implied odds in source or lifted into GSE.

assumptions: The comparisons establish where iWAR improves team-level accounting and provide a reproducible set of aggregate results, but leave the allocation of individual credit as a separate empirical question; individual performance has no observed ground-truth WAR label, and the bWAR agreement analysis (RA correlation 0.934, MAE 0.406 wins; FIP 0.916, MAE 0.449) documents broad agreement while leaving individual correctness open.

layer2.mapping: The individual-credit humility is the same no-ground-truth-label honesty GSE attaches to player valuation.
layer2.telemetry: team accounting improved; individual credit separate empirical question; no ground-truth WAR label; bWAR agreement RA corr 0.934/MAE 0.406, FIP 0.916/0.449

reasoning_traces.think: The retrocausal genealogy of this paper is the matched historical benchmark of wins above replacement. Michael Doane, an independent researcher in Cary, North Carolina, posting to arXiv in 2026, introduces iWAR, a system estimating wins above replacement from historical Retrosheet play-by-play records in runs-allowed and fielding-independent pitching versions, and compares it against Baseball-Reference WAR, FanGraphs WAR, and run-based alternatives on identical team-seasons. The work sits in the lineage of Baumer, Jensen, and Matthews's openWAR with its conservation-of-runs framework and resampling uncertainty, Brill and Wyner's Grid WAR for nonlinear starting-pitcher valuation, Jensen, Shirley, and Wyner's Bayesball fielding model, and the broader cross-era Full House Modeling, alongside Shmueli's distinction between description and prediction, Gneiting's forecast-evaluation principles, Künsch's block bootstrap for dependent observations, and Grinsztajn's demonstration that tree-based models still beat deep learning on tabular data. The recursive theory of mind is the WAR accounting pipeline and its two evaluation targets. Batting weights come from same-season run expectancy over base-out states, an event's run value being the runs scored plus the change in expected runs remaining; pitching is either runs-allowed, expected runs over actual outs minus charged runs with park and defense adjustment, or fielding-independent, the numerator thirteen home runs plus three walks and hit batters minus two strikeouts; replacement contributes zero point two zero six wins per team-game so that centered league WAR sums to zero point two zero six times games, and the fixed map converts WAR per game to a winning fraction by adding zero point two nine four. The crucial conceptual move is to separate reconstruction, where predictor and outcome refer to the same completed season, from replay, where origin-year WAR predicts the next season's record, because a measure that fits a completed season closely may preserve information that is weakly persistent into the following year. Cross-layer veto adjudication is the matched results and their sensitivity to conversion and coverage. On the common sample of one thousand four hundred seventy-one team-seasons across seventy-nine years, iWAR RA reconstructs the completed season with mean absolute error three point six nine five credited wins per one hundred sixty-two games versus four point seven two four for bWAR and four point seven four four for fWAR, roughly a twenty-two percent reduction that survives scalar calibration almost unchanged. Yet PythagenPat reconstructs records more closely than every WAR measure, and next-season replay reverses the story: the fixed RA-minus-fWAR difference is positive but flips negative after calibration on identical rows, so the conversion itself changes the ordering. The advantage is concentrated in early history and shrinks when the bWAR comparison expands to one hundred eighteen years, and a bounded learned-model study finds the neural ensemble worse than the development-selected ridge comparator, with the ordering even reversing on a small descriptive subset. The implementation invariants map directly onto GSE. The run-expectancy batting weights and event run-value decomposition are GSE's base-out expected-points kernel; the reconstruction-versus-replay separation is GSE's description-versus-prediction evaluation discipline; the per-method intercept-and-slope calibration is GSE's calibration-map fix; and the five-thousand-draw calendar-block bootstrap is GSE's dependence-aware inference, the same lesson as the DLS match-clustered bootstrap and the field-hockey small-sample shrinkage already in the corpus. The conserving pitching-fielding transfer, which leaves the team total unchanged, is GSE's attribution-identifiability limit: improved team reconstruction cannot validate individual credit, and the paper honestly leaves individual allocation as a separate empirical question with no ground-truth WAR label. The outputs are team win reconstructions from play-by-play data; GSE lifts no sportsbook lines, spreads, totals, or implied odds. The accounting and uncertainty results make the benchmark rigorous and bounded. The exact identity decomposing the WAR-versus-run-based mean squared error into a squared prediction distance plus an error cross-term locates iWAR RA's advantage in its closer proximity to the observed-run expectation, with every method's negative cross-term partly offsetting its distance; but a causal allocation among parks, replacement, batting, and defense is impossible without a complete aligned provider component ledger. The conditional intervals deliberately omit method-development, source-revision, and coefficient-fitting uncertainty, provider one-decimal rounding is propagated as a separate bound, and era groups lack enough five-year blocks for resolved intervals, so the pooled interval combines observed history rather than yielding five separate era conclusions. The caveats close the account with the data-integrity and scope limits that define the paper's honesty. Record discrepancies between event files and game logs are retained without inferred repair, missing provider values stay missing with no imputed replacement, and FanGraphs' retroactive Statcast revisions mean current-vintage provider WAR may differ from archived season-end values that were unavailable; the methods were developed before the expanded benchmark so project-wide independence cannot be claimed, and the learned-model study was amended after a constant-detector numerical defect, making it amended historical evidence rather than an untouched holdout. The invariant for GSE is to carry the run-expectancy valuation, the reconstruction-versus-replay target separation, the scalar-calibration sensitivity check, the calendar-block inference, and the conserving-transfer attribution limit while recording the missing-data honesty, the provider-vintage caution, and the doctrine that a credible assessment must name the target, report the conversion, and show which historical observations support the conclusion, treating simple run-based baselines as demanding comparators that elaborate WAR totals do not automatically beat. The replay itself is bounded: roster turnover, aging, injuries and player-level projections are absent, and the chronological scalar fit prevents later outcomes from entering the fit without reconstructing the information actually available to an analyst at each historical date, so a genuine as-of-date forecast study would still require archived inputs and a clearly defined forecast date.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Matched historical benchmark of WAR. Michael Doane, Independent Researcher Cary NC; ORCID 0009-0003-0521-8981; arXiv 2026. iWAR from Retrosheet play-by-play (RA + FIP versions) vs bWAR/fWAR/run-based on identical team-seasons. Lineage: openWAR (Baumer-Jensen-Matthews 2015 JQAS, conservation-of-runs + resampling), Grid WAR (Brill-Wyner 2024 JQAS, nonlinear pitcher), Bayesball (Jensen-Shirley-Wyner 2009 AOAS), Full House Modeling (Yan 2025 cross-era); Shmueli 2010 (explain/predict), Gneiting 2011 (forecast eval), Künsch 1989 (block bootstrap), Grinsztajn-Oyallon-Varoquaux 2022 (trees vs deep tabular), Miller 2007 (Pythagorean derivation). Code github MRDOANE/iwar-historical-benchmark, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23455100.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Batting weights from same-season run expectancy (base-out states); event run value = runs scored + change in expected runs remaining. RA pitching = expected runs over actual outs - charged runs (league env + park factor; fielding support subtracted = assigned to fielders). FIP numerator 13*HR+3*(BB+HBP)-2*K (incl IBB/inside-park HR; league constant; no infield flies/park/leverage). Replacement 0.206 wins/team-game (57% batting/43% pitching); sum WAR=0.206 sum G; +0.294 -> implied wins half both-teams games. Credited yi=(Wi+0.5Ti)/Gi; fixed map y-hat=0.294+WARi/Gi; error 162(y-hat-y). Pythagorean RS^2/(RS^2+RA^2); PythagenPat gamma=[(RS+RA)/G]^0.285. Calibration yi=alpha+beta*xi (OLS unclipped); same-season leave-one-year-out, replay expanding strictly-earlier (>=10 years+150 pairs). 5000 draws 5-yr calendar blocks anchored 1908 (>=10 blocks). MSE_WAR-MSE_R=mean(d^2)+2mean(eR*d). Equations math-font reconstructed.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Common 1471 team-seasons/79 yr/1441 pairs: RA recon MAE 3.695 vs bWAR 4.724/fWAR 4.744 (-21.8%/-22.1%), paired -1.030/-1.049 CI [-1.367,-0.706]/[-1.398,-0.725]; calibration preserves (RA diffs -1.027/-1.025). PythagenPat beats EVERY WAR (3.263/4.122). Replay sign-flip: RA-fWAR fixed +0.231 -> calibrated -0.148 on identical 1282 rows (conversion effect). Era: 1908-1945 -1.525 largest, 2015-2025 -0.058 smallest; broader 118-yr bWAR smaller (-0.697). Neural WORSE than ridge (replay 10.163 vs 9.946, +0.217 [0.015,0.474]; 504-pair subset reversed). Conserving pitching-fielding transfer -> team total invariant -> team reconstruction can't validate individual credit (no ground-truth WAR label; bWAR agreement RA corr 0.934). Missing retained no repair; FanGraphs Statcast retroactive 2016; conditional intervals omit method-dev/source-revision/coeff-fitting; amended after constant-detector defect. Doctrine: name target, report conversion, show observations. Zero sportsbook lines lifted.

universal_lens: A matched historical benchmark of wins above replacement introduces iWAR (from Retrosheet play-by-play, in runs-allowed and fielding-independent versions) and shows it reconstructs completed team records ~22% more accurately than bWAR/fWAR on 1,471 common team-seasons, an advantage that survives scalar calibration but is beaten by the simpler PythagenPat run-based reference, reverses under next-season replay calibration on identical rows, concentrates in early history, and shrinks with broader coverage; a bounded learned-model study finds neural ensembles worse than ridge, and the paper's central doctrine is that a credible WAR assessment must name the target (reconstruction vs replay), report the conversion, and show which historical observations support the conclusion, while conserving pitching-fielding transfers leave individual credit allocation a separate empirical question.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats iWAR (Retrosheet PBP; RA + FIP) vs bWAR/fWAR/run-based on identical rows (common 1471 team-seasons/79 yr/1441 pairs; secondary 2554/118 yr); batting weights from run expectancy (base-out), event run value = runs scored + change in expected runs remaining; RA = expected runs over outs - charged (park + defense); FIP 13*HR+3*(BB+HBP)-2*K; replacement 0.206 wins/team-game (57/43), sum WAR=0.206 sum G; yi=(W+0.5T)/G, fixed map y-hat=0.294+WAR/G, error 162(y-hat-y); Pythagorean RS^2/(RS^2+RA^2), PythagenPat gamma=[(RS+RA)/G]^0.285; calibration yi=alpha+beta*xi (OLS), same-season leave-one-year-out / replay expanding strictly-earlier (>=10 yr+150 pairs, 1282 pairs); 5000 draws 5-yr calendar blocks anchored 1908 (Künsch, >=10 blocks), conditional intervals omit method-dev/source-revision/coeff-fitting; RA recon MAE 3.695 vs 4.724/4.744 (~22%, paired -1.030/-1.049), calibration preserves; PythagenPat beats every WAR (3.263); replay RA-fWAR sign-flip +0.231->-0.148 identical rows; era 1908-1945 -1.525 / 2015-2025 -0.058; broader bWAR -0.697 smaller; neural worse ridge (10.163 vs 9.946, +0.217 [0.015,0.474]); MSE_WAR-MSE_R=mean(d^2)+2mean(eR*d); conserving pitching-fielding transfer team-total invariant -> individual credit not identifiable (no ground-truth label, bWAR corr 0.934); missing no repair, FanGraphs Statcast retroactive; name target/report conversion/show observations; equations math-font reconstructed.
gse_mapping: GSE lifts the run-expectancy base-out EP kernel and event run-value decomposition, the reconstruction-versus-replay (description-vs-prediction) target separation, the per-method scalar calibration as its calibration-map fix with mapping-sensitivity sign-flip awareness, the calendar-block bootstrap as its dependence-aware inference (same as DLS match-bootstrap and field-hockey small-sample), the Pythagorean/PythagenPat simple-baseline comparator that elaborate WAR does not automatically beat, and the conserving-transfer attribution-identifiability limit (team reconstruction cannot validate individual credit); treats the missing-data no-repair policy, provider-vintage caution, conditional-interval scope, and amended-holdout honesty as data-integrity discipline, and the name-the-target/report-the-conversion/show-the-observations doctrine as its evaluation-honesty rule; all outputs are team win reconstructions from play-by-play data, never sportsbook lines, and individual credit remains a separate empirical question with no ground-truth label.
